issues.legal_issue: A pending appeal does not abate when a transferee already on the record represents the deceased appellant’s estate in respect of the property in dispute.
material_facts: The transferee of the property was already joined as a co-appellant in the second appeal with the vendor.
The vendor died while the second appeal was pending.
The transferee was on the record and represented the deceased appellant’s estate as to the property in dispute.
The High Court held that the appeal had abated and that the transferee could not be brought on record as the deceased appellant’s legal representative.
issues.conclusion: The appeal had not abated; the transferee was entitled to prosecute it without a separate application to bring the deceased appellant’s legal representatives on record. The High Court’s order was set aside and the appeal was remitted for disposal according to law.
issues.legal_principle: A transferee of property who is already on the record may, at least as an intermeddler, be treated as the deceased appellant’s legal representative in respect of that property. If the deceased appellant’s estate in the property is already represented, a separate application to bring legal representatives on record is unnecessary and the appeal does not abate. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for this principle.

rule.if: second_appeal_pending and deceased_appellant and transferee_already_on_record and estate_represented_as_to_disputed_property

predicates.second_appeal_pending: A second appeal was pending when an appellant died.
predicates.deceased_appellant: An appellant died while the appeal was pending.
predicates.transferee_already_on_record: A person who had received the disputed property from the appellant was already on the record as a co-appellant.
predicates.estate_represented_as_to_disputed_proper: The person on the record represented the deceased appellant’s estate in relation to the disputed property.
predicates.appeal_not_abated_and_transferee_may_pro: The appeal has not abated and the transferee may prosecute it.

issues.definition: When an appellant dies during a pending second appeal and a transferee already on the record represents the deceased’s estate as to the disputed property, the appeal does not abate and the transferee may prosecute it.
